The cargo liaison on cleaning rounds
This section shows what the desk expects
Companion Animal Travel Desk handling
This section explains how the Companion Animal Travel Desk keeps each animal trip calm, accurate, and ready for boarding.

The desk starts with steady listening. Staff confirm the travel plan, note any care needs, and pass comfort details to the welfare coordinator before anything is finalized. Each record should reflect the animal's species, temperament, and general comfort needs so the next team can prepare the right space and handling approach. When the traveler arrives, the welcome team should already know what support is needed and should keep the handoff smooth and respectful. Care plans must stay practical, clear, and easy for the boarding team to follow.

Staff should use plain language with travelers, avoid rushed promises, and correct mistakes as soon as they are found. If an animal seems stressed, the desk should slow the process, alert the proper teammate, and avoid adding extra noise or movement around the carrier. Keep carrier labels readable, check that documents match the booking, and make sure any feeding or resting notes are shared with the right people. If a traveler like Zain Bianchi or Sofia Park mentions changes in the pet's routine, update the file before the animal moves on. If Ruby is traveling, the same careful review applies.

The desk also keeps the area tidy and ready for the next case. Staff should clear used forms, return supplies to their place, and leave counters free of clutter so the welcome team can work without delay. Calm habits matter here because they help people trust the process and help animals settle more easily.

If anything seems unclear, contact the senior coordinator or the welfare coordinator at Aurelia Skyways.
